title: NAT handoff TLS probe - incident scratchpad
content:
Summary / quick notes:
- Sporadic TLS handshake failures from private-deploy nodes to external API endpoints (external vendor A). Failures primarily show "tlsv1 alert unknown ca" or timeout on SNI stage. Customer reports calls fail ~10% of the time during high egress short-burst traffic.
- Suspect NAT gateway / SNAT port exhaustion + path MTU / UDP-based DNS fragmentation issues causing wrong certificate selection or failing SNI. Also possible asymmetric routing via Transit Gateway + firewall device.

Observed behavior (2026-02-27 through 2026-02-29):
- Failures concentrated on two private clusters in us-west-2, both using NAT Gateway + a shared central egress appliance via Transit Gateway.
- When failures occur, TCP handshake usually completes, but TLS ClientHello is not acknowledged by server (server either sends RST or nothing). Some traces show server responded but with unexpected cert (mismatch).
- DNS lookups sometimes returned truncated responses (TC=1) when query size > 512. We see retries switching to TCP in some clients, not all.

Timeline (brief):
- 2026-02-27 09:43: first reports from ops automated checks (5m spike).
- 2026-02-27 10:05 manual curl from customer node reproduces ~1/5 failures.
- 2026-02-28 15:12 added tcpdump capture and conntrack logs.
- 2026-02-29 08:30 rolled a NAT gateway replacement on one VPC -> reduction of failures but not elimination.

Commands / snippets tried locally (notes):
- curl failing example:
  curl -v --resolve api.vendor-a.com:443:34.201.100.12 https://api.vendor-a.com/health || true
  * TCP_NODELAY set
  * Connected to api.vendor-a.com (34.201.100.12) port 443 (#0)
  * ALPN, offering h2
  * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, ClientHello (1)
  * error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert unknown ca
  * Closing connection 0
  => Not consistent; sometimes returns 200.

- openssl s_client (when failing):
  openssl s_client -connect api.vendor-a.com:443 -servername api.vendor-a.com -msg -debug
  >>> TLS 1.3, Handshake, ClientHello
  read R BLOCK
  TLS alert read:warning:unknown CA
  write to 0x7f...:errno=104
  -> look for middlebox injecting alerts or editing handshake.

- tcpdump around failure (captured on node ENI):
  tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/fail.pcap host 34.201.100.12 and port 443
  Brief observ: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK (3-way ok), ClientHello sent, then either no ServerHello or RST from server IP. In other captures, see ServerHello but cert with CN mismatch (points to internal appliance cert).

- capture at NAT gateway (flow logs / VPC):
  Flow logs show connections allowed, NAT translations present. No obvious RST spike, but ephemeral port reuse high.

- conntrack on appliance (iptables/nf_conntrack):
  # conntrack -L | grep 34.201.100.12 | tail -n 20
  tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.0.7.92 dst=34.201.100.12 sport=34578 dport=443 packets=120 bytes=31200 ...
  tcp      6 29 SYN_SENT src=10.0.7.93 dst=34.201.100.12 sport=45612 dport=443 packets=1 bytes=60 ...
  Observed many TIME_WAIT / CLOSE_WAIT entries; transient port exhaustion possible.

- check iptables rules for masquerade / hairpin:
  iptables -t nat -S | sed -n '1,120p'
  -A POSTROUTING -s 10.0.0.0/16 -o eth1 -j MASQUERADE
  No special mangle rules.

- dig results showing truncation (from node):
  dig +short api.vendor-a.com @10.0.0.10 A
  ;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 0
  ;; got answer: truncation
  Follow-up with +tcp shows full answer. Some clients don't retry TCP.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) NAT port exhaustion or connection tracking collisions: when SNAT ports exhausted, connection reuse or incorrect mapping may forward traffic to egress appliance control plane, causing wrong cert / close. Replacement reduced but didn't fix -> partially supports.
2) Asymmetric routing through transit appliance: egress path sometimes hits firewall/proxy that does TLS interception (internal cert) causing unknown CA on client side. Intermittency fits occasional policy routing by load-balancer.
3) DNS truncation causes clients to fallback to wrong IP (via stub resolver behavior) leading to backend mismatch / SNI mismatch. Fragmentation on UDP (EDNS0 large responses) could be lost at middlebox.
4) MTU / TCP MSS clamping issue causing ClientHello fragmentation or middlebox drop; rare but can manifest as TLS handshake stalls.

Evidence for/against: 
- For 1: High ephemeral port reuse in conntrack, NAT gateway replacement lowered error rate.
- Against 1: AWS NAT Gateway normally has huge port pool; but shared egress appliance might be using single NAT device with limited ports.
- For 2: Captures showing internal cert indicates interception for some flows. But interception not consistent across flows -> likely conditional (eg based on port or SNI).
- For 3: dig shows truncation on UDP; vendor DNS provider has large TXT records historically; some private CNAME chains produce larger responses.

Repro instructions (quick):
1) From affected node 10.0.7.92 run: curl -v --resolve api.vendor-a.com:443:34.201.100.12 https://api.vendor-a.com/health  -o /dev/null -s -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}
"  repeat 100 times in loop and log failures.
2) Simultaneously run tcpdump on node and on egress appliance to correlate.
3) Use dig +bufsize=4096 and +tcp to see EDNS behavior.

Quick mitigation tried:
- Replaced NAT gateway in one VPC -> reduced errors by ~40% during a 6-hour window.
- Added temporary iptables conntrack helpers to reduce TIME_WAIT retention on appliance (set nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait lower) -> seemed to help short-term but needs caution.
- Forced clients to use TCP DNS (not ideal) via resolver policy on nodes -> removed truncation driven failures in limited test.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Talk to network infra (Transit GW owners) to check for conditional proxying rules or TLS inspection policies; share pcap evidence. (Marco)
- [ ] Confirm NAT port utilization metrics on shared egress device during incident windows. Look for ephemeral port exhaustion alerts. (Priya)
- [ ] Ask vendor A if they're seeing health checks / SYNs from unexpected IPs or any middlebox logs. (Evan)
- [ ] Short-term: add resolver config to prefer TCP for vendor-a queries on affected clusters (requires rollout to config management). Measure impact. (Evan)
- [ ] Create regression test: synthetic high-concurrency TLS bursts to vendor-a endpoints to reproduce under load. (eng-private-deploy)
- [ ] Audit EDNS0/UDP buffer sizes; consider adding DNS proxy that enforces TCP fallback.

Notes to self (scratchy):
- Check Transit Gateway route table for blackhole routes or ECMP groups that might shuffle egress across appliances.
- Look up INF-2147 (related egress appliance capacity planning).
- Slack logs: thread C01ABCDEF timestamp 1670000000000000 has early captures.

Appendix: useful commands (copyable)
- while true; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" https://api.vendor-a.com/health; sleep 0.2; done
- sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/pending.pcap host api.vendor-a.com and port 443
- sudo conntrack -L | grep 34.201.100.12 | wc -l
- dig +bufsize=4096 api.vendor-a.com @10.0.0.10

End of scratchpad.
